disease.basis: SIM MODEL simplified communicable-disease simulation (owner spec: configurable epidemiological parameters; scenario outputs are NOT real medical predictions). Transmission runs over real contact structure only — household co-residents and a seeded sample of institution-mates — never over invented contact networks. Noncommunicable disease is the chronic pathway of the age-related cause (GDD-12 §3.4), recorded on health profiles.
disease.scenarios_note: Configurable disease scenarios fired deterministically by day_index (e.g. an index case for tests), in the government-config scenarios pattern. Empty by default — no outbreak is invented for the standard world beyond the labelled endemic index chance above.

surveillance.basis: SIM MODEL public-health thresholds, measured monthly from disease_records: when active cases per 100 residents in a city reach the threshold, the city's facility runs a vaccination campaign from its own budget (vaccine doses in stock bound how many residents can be covered) and the event is recorded.

education.basis: SIM MODEL education framework. Institution types, capacities and operating budgets have no design-data basis (GDD-11 fixes the institutions that exist and that they are civic, not their budgets). Curricula subjects/objectives are configuration in the spec's shape; the skills they write are the canonical character_skills vocabulary (GDD-11 §4) and the GDD-11 caps (school 20 / college 24) remain contract in education.py, untouched by this file.

calendar.basis: SIM MODEL academic calendar on the sim's 30-day months: a 12-month academic year with a term examination in months 3, 6, 9 and 12 of each year (month_index % 3 == 0).

doctor.objectives: Structure of the human body (simulated curriculum)

dropout.basis: SIM MODEL justified-dropout rules, read from measured records only: a school student aged 14+ leaves when their household's finances record debt in two consecutive monthly snapshots AND their latest examination average (or performance, pre-exam) is below the pass mark; a college student leaves after two consecutive months of measured attendance below the floor. Dropout is a recorded status with its cause, never a dice roll against a child.

examinations.basis: SIM MODEL examination model. A result is a pure function of measured inputs — the record's attendance rate, the student's per-subject proficiency, the assigned teacher's latest evaluation at the institution, and the institution building's measured condition — plus a seeded jitter keyed by (exam, student, subject). Same stored inputs always reproduce the same result (acceptance criterion 5); no grade is ever assigned without those inputs.

framework.authority: Ministry of Education (GOV-EDUCATION, Session 05 institutions table)
framework.note: The world's schools and college are civic (city-owned, GDD-02 §6). No private institution exists in the building data, so none operates; the framework records the sector list the data model supports.

learning.basis: SIM MODEL learning rates. Proficiency (0-100 per subject, learning_records) grows from MEASURED attendance and the assigned teacher's measured evaluation; it is a record of study, not a second skill system — character_skills writes remain education.py's, under the GDD-11 caps.

teachers.basis: SIM MODEL staffing rule. Teachers are real citizens employed as the teacher profession (genesis, Session 04 civic labour, Session 05 civil service). Assignment is by residence city; in Rupsha the college takes lecturer posts first (1 per 10 enrolled college students, at least 1 while anyone is enrolled), the rest teach at the school. Evaluations are computed from the institution's measured student outcomes (examination means and attendance) — never asserted.

health.basis: SIM MODEL simplified health rules implementing GDD-12's design contract (condition = band + cause + course + memory; the cause list is CLOSED — a condition may only arise from a system the project has designed, plus Session 06's disease system, which is the system that causes its cause). These rules are a simulation model, NOT clinical knowledge: no real disease is named, no real treatment is described, and no output is a medical prediction.

life_stage_care.basis: SIM MODEL care pathways tied to Session 01 life-cycle records: a birth life-event in the month produces a maternal + infant care record at the mother's city facility (consuming a maternal kit when stocked); elders with a chronic profile receive a monthly chronic review visit (consuming a chronic pack); enrolled children receive a child health check each exam term. All are records of care delivered by the real facility, capacity permitting.

medications.basis: FICTIONAL simulated medication inventory (owner spec): invented product names for an inventory simulation, carrying quantities and the clinic's internal procurement rates only. Nothing here is a real medicine, a real price, or medical advice; care is free at point of use and no patient is ever charged.

mortality.basis: GDD-12 §3.4: the death rule reads elder stage PLUS active/recent serious conditions. SIM MODEL multiplier applied to lifecycle.death_probability for an Elder with an active or recovering serious condition; 1.0 (no change) for everyone else and in worlds without the Session 06 layer.

onset_daily.basis: SIM MODEL daily onset probabilities per living character, rolled on seeded streams. Weather causes read the day's persisted weather preset and its gameplay flags (the same flags GDD-07 reads).

profiles.basis: SIM MODEL health-profile aggregation. health_score (0-100) is a monthly aggregate of measured state — the needs system's healthcare/sleep/food satisfactions, age band, active conditions, chronic status — computed by a documented formula in health.py. It is a simulation index, not a medical assessment of any person.

recovery_days.basis: GDD-12 §4's tuning for treated windows (unwell 1-3, injured 3-7, serious 7+); untreated windows for injured/serious are SIM MODEL extensions of GDD-12's unwell 3-6. A failed diagnosis lengthens the treated window by the diagnosis_failure_factor (GDD-12 §4.3).

humandev.basis: SIM MODEL human-development measurement. Every indicator is computed from persistent simulation records by the documented formulas in humandev.py (METHODOLOGY); life expectancy is reported two ways — the observed mean age at death over recorded deaths, and a model estimate integrated from lifecycle.py's own mortality curve — and the composite HDI is the geometric mean of health, education and income indices, each defined in humandev.py. Nothing is interpolated: a component that cannot be computed is absent, not estimated.

notes: Session 06 education / healthcare / human-development configuration. Everything in this file is CONFIGURATION, not code, in the government-config.json pattern. Institution and facility identities are grounded in the project's own building data (buildings-district1.json + city2-shibnagar.json); every rate, capacity, budget, probability and cost that has no basis in the merged design data is a simulation rule labelled SIM MODEL in the section's basis field and can be changed without touching engine code. NO prices are defined here for care or education: both are civic and free at point of use (GDD-11 §7, GDD-12 §6); the medication unit costs below are the clinic's internal procurement rates against the market pool (the Session 03 road-repair-rate precedent), never a charge to any patient. Canonical wages stay in prices.json; canonical profession facts stay in professions.json.

research.basis: SIM MODEL research ecosystem at the District College (the only higher-education institution in the building data; the framework supports universities where a later district builds one). Projects are led by real lecturer citizens, funded from a configured share of the college's monthly civic budget, run a configured number of months, and complete into research_records (publications as simulated records). Completion raises the college's measured research capability, which feeds its institution performance — the configurable institutional-development effect the spec requires.
